newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold says Stop & Shop deal better than expected.
newsitem.headline: Ahold says Stop & Shop deal better than expected.

text.p: Ahold's recent acquisition of U.S. Stop & Shop is proceeding better than exected, Ahold USA President Rob Zwartendijk said on Thursday.
"There have been no negative surprises. Things are working out better than expected, to put it mildly," Zwartendijk told a news conference to present the group's second quarter results.
"We are looking forward to exploiting the great many synergies there," he added.
Group President Cees Van der Hoeven was similarly upbeat about the deal, saying it would lead to a direct improvement in group earnings per share.
"At this moment it seems the acquisition of Stop & Shop will directly lead to an improvement in EPS, even after the recent major share issue," Van der Hoeven told the conference.
Earlier, Ahold announced a 20 percent increase in operating results for the U.S., with its Tops and Edwards stores showing particular growth.
Van der Hoeven said the recently announced reorganisation within Ahold USA -- the merger of Finast with Tops, and Edwards with Giant -- would result in 400 job losses in total.
The axe will fall among the 900 workers at the head offices of Edwards in Long Island and Finast in Cleveland which are both to be closed, Zwartendijk said.
Ahold is the fourth largest retailer in the U.S. with 800 stores generating a turnover of $14 billion, more than half of total group turnover.

Zwartendijk said Ahold was still on the lookout for acquisitions on the East coast of the U.S. "We're not going to look at the West coast because we wouldn't be able to exploit synergies from there," he said.
Ahold earlier announced an 18 percent rise in group net profit in the second quarter to 121.3 million guilders.
